title: Cross-protocol inference surface PRD and launch slices
creator: Alicia Park
description: Product requirements and acceptance criteria for a single, cross-protocol hosted inference surface that cleanly exposes chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank capabilities under a consistent behavior contract. This PRD documents the slices for a phased launch, behavioral guards, compatibility rules, and the launch checklist for operations and GD/SE teams.
goals: Provide a single surface where SDK/REST callers can target chat, completion, embeddings or rerank with predictable semantics and consistent error modes
Define minimal behavioral contracts for deterministic rollback and canary paths (nondeterministic outputs allowed but quality/regression metrics required)
Ship a launch-slice that supports: chat with streaming, completion with structured output, embeddings v1, and rerank baseline (synchronous)
Ensure launch observability and guardrails so customer-facing regressions are detectable within the first 30 minutes of traffic shifts
non_goals: Full polyglot multimodal surface (images/audio) — out of scope for this slice
Support for every legacy endpoint alias; we will map high-use aliases only
On-prem private deployment packaging for this launch — Private will follow in next cycle
success_metrics: Latency: P95 token-latency for chat <= 150ms on 8k seq for hosted tier
Error rate: API 5xx <= 0.1% in steady-state for first 7 days post-launch
Quality baselines: Embeddings cosine stability > 0.98 vs canary eval set; rerank NDCG drop <= 1.5% vs baseline
Adoption: 1,000 active API keys using new surface within 30 days
scope: Streaming support for chat only in slice-1; completion streaming is deferred
Structured output: JSON schema enforcement and schema-version header for completions
Auth: existing API key flows only. SSO/tenanted RBAC deferred
Telemetry: token-level cost attribution, per-route latency histograms, per-model quality counters
assumptions: Underlying runtime kernels in runtime-2.1 will support kv-cache snapshotting required by chat streaming
Dedicated capacity contracts are not required for initial hosted customers of this surface
Model catalog includes at least one vetted model per capability (chat/completion/embed/rerank) at launch
high_level_design: Router: single entrypoint /v1/inference with route-based dispatch to capability-specific handlers
Capability adapters: thin adapters that normalize request/response shape and apply behavior guards
Behavioral layer: preflight checks (prompt length, token budget), fallback policies (model downgrade) and quality gating
Observability: sampling for full prompt/response traces (redact PII) and metrics emitted to telemetry pipeline
api_contracts: Chat: POST /v1/inference/chat -> body: {model, messages, max_tokens, stream:false|true, temperature, top_p, metadata}, response: streaming chunks with event types [delta, done, error]
Completions: POST /v1/inference/completions -> body: {model, prompt, output_schema_version, max_tokens, stop}, response: {choices: [{text, structured_output}], usage}
Embeddings: POST /v1/inference/embeddings -> body: {model, inputs:[string], dimension_profile}, response: {data:[{embedding, index}], usage}
Rerank: POST /v1/inference/rerank -> body: {model, query, candidates:[{id, text, metadata}]}, response: {ranked_ids:[id], scores}
Errors: unified error envelope {code, message, retryable:true|false, details:url} and HTTP status mapping (400,401,403,404,429,500)
Headers: X-Redwood-Model-Version, X-Trace-Id, X-Cost-Estimate required for billing simulation in canary
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end: a new API key can call all four routes in slice-1 and receive responses conforming to contracts above
Behavioral: prompt truncation and 'token_budget_exceeded' error is returned consistently for long prompts across all capabilities
Streaming: chat streaming produces chunks within expected heartbeat interval (<200ms) and resumes after transient reconnects
Quality: embeddings similarity test suite passes (example queries stored in /confluence/unified_surface/embeddings_suite) with cosine thresholds
Operational: rollout health criteria: rolling deploy must maintain 99.9% of baseline success rate and auto-rollback on sustained 1% absolute error increase over 15 minutes
Security: all sampled request/response traces have PII redaction applied before being persisted
Docs: public API docs published with examples for each route and a migration guide for legacy endpoints
SDKs: Node/Go SDKs updated with new route wrappers and included in smoke-test CI
launch_checklist: PRD approval: PM+Design+Eng sign-off (documented in Confluence)
API schema freeze and OpenAPI spec committed (github.com/redwood-inference/api-defs/pull/742)
E2E tests green for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank both in staging and canary
Canary run at 5% traffic for 48 hours with daily quality checks
Runbook: incident runbook written and reviewed by SRE (runbook link in Confluence)
Billing simulation: cost-estimate header validated and usage accounting spot-checked
Support: KB article and triage playbook published for CS and Solutions Eng
Postmortem cadence: 72-hour review scheduled if any quality/regression alert fires during rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Staging): integration testing and SDK smoke tests only
Phase 1 (Canary): 5% traffic, internal customers + targeted external beta for 48 hours
Phase 2 (Incremental): 25% traffic over next 24 hours if metrics stable
Phase 3 (General): full rollout with burst controls and regional fallback enabled
Fallback policy: automatic model downgrade to verified fallback variant; if error rate persists for 30 minutes, rollback to previous deployment
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: embeddings drift vs existing surface leading to customer regressions -> Mitigation: gated eval suite, ability to pin model versions per-tenant
Risk: streaming connection churn causing higher ops load -> Mitigation: circuit-breaker at gateway and backoff guidance in SDK
Risk: unforeseen cost spike due to batching changes -> Mitigation: billing simulation and soft quota enforcement in canary
Risk: inconsistency in structured output across languages -> Mitigation: add localization tests to acceptance suite
open_questions: Q1: Should rerank support async batching for large candidate sets at launch? (Eng to advise by 2026-03-17)
Q2: Do we require schema-version negotiation header for embeddings v1 or embed versioning only via model tag? (Product decision)
Q3: What is the SLA statement we publish for this surface at GA (SRE + Legal to confirm)
Q4: Can we reuse existing rate-limit buckets or do we need new per-route buckets for cost isolation?
